How to use this site

This set contains 6000 study entries. It includes single words, noun phrases, verb forms, useful expressions, question patterns, and sentence patterns. That makes it useful for real A1-A2 reading and speaking practice, not just memorizing isolated words.

Recommended routine: learn 25 new words, mark them as known, then use flashcards and quiz mode.

Quick study tips for low A2

What should I learn first?

Start with A1 and A1-A2 entries. Focus on people, home, food, time, travel, school, important verbs, expressions, and questions.

Should I memorize full phrases?

Yes. For speaking, phrases like j’ai besoin de..., je voudrais..., and où est...? are often more useful than single words alone.

How do I use “type” and “function”?

Type tells you what the word is: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, expression. Function tells you how it works in a sentence.

Suggested 7-day method

Day 1: Learn 25 nouns and phrases. Say each word out loud.
Day 2: Review yesterday. Add 25 verbs or verb forms.
Day 3: Use quiz mode for 10 minutes.
Day 4: Learn 25 adjectives and make simple sentences: La maison est grande.
Day 5: Learn 25 expressions. Use them in mini dialogues.
Day 6: Review only unknown words.
Day 7: Favorite difficult words and review them again.
